column4: This verse says faces are humbled before the Ever-Living, linking the section's lowered gaze to a broader posture of submission on the Day; its own contribution is the face's abasement before God.
The section's source gloss connects looking with sight and insight; this verse contrasts whoever sees with whoever is blind, making explicit the boundary between perception and mere looking.
This verse asks whether people see that God created livestock for them; it gives a direct animal-creation counterpart to the camel the section invites them to inspect.
This verse asks readers to see birds held in the sky, adding a specific creature-in-the-sky scene beside the section's camel and raised-sky view.
This verse makes stars signs for finding one's way through land and sea at night, connecting the section's upward look at the sky with orientation on the earth below.
This verse asks whether people see that God begins creation and repeats it; the next 29:20 adds travel across the earth to inspect how creation began, tying visible creation to return.
This verse joins life emerging from death to earth revived after death and says people will be brought forth likewise, a specific earth-and-resurrection parallel to the section's gaze.
Before 30:50 tells people to look at God's mercy in reviving earth, this verse contributes the winds, clouds, and rain that make the land revive.
After 30:50's revived earth, this verse adds the contrary sight of vegetation yellowing after a wind; it also says the viewers remain ungrateful.
This verse calls the revived dead land and its grain a sign; the next 36:34 adds gardens and springs, so this ayah contributes the earth-revival scene beside the section's spring image.
Before 40:19 names God's knowledge of furtive eyes, this verse contributes the approaching Day, with hearts at throats and people in dread, grounding the hidden glance in judgment.
The section's eye image includes humbled sight and paradise; this verse says eyes delight in the garden's provision, a specific afterlife reversal from the downcast gaze.

The source section's root خ ش ع is glossed through a gaze lowered to earth; this verse uses that root for humility in prayer, a devotional counterpart to the humbled gaze, though it does not itself mention the eyes.
